heroHeadline: PLA 16 Sorties May 23 (13 Cross N/C/SW/E — 4-Sector Surge on Day WaPo Confirms $14B Arms Pause); 4 Sorties May 24 (Pullback); Finance Committee Hearings Tomorrow; 7 Days to HIMARS Deadline
heroSubtitle: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 16 PLA aircraft sorties on May 23, 2026 — 13 crossing the median line into northern, central, southwestern, and eastern ADIZ sectors simultaneously — the same four-sector blockade-rehearsal geometry seen on May 20 (24 sorties) and May 7 (22 sorties). The surge coincided precisely with the Washington Post confirming that the Trump administration has paused the $14 billion Taiwan arms sale (PAC-3 MSE interceptors and NASAMS) following the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14-15), with Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao citing munitions drawdown from Operation Epic Fury (Iran). Taiwan responded with 'no notification received' and maintained an optimistic posture. On May 24, PLA activity pulled back to 4 sorties (3 crossing SW/SE ADIZ) and 6 PLAN vessels — consistent with the established spike-then-pullback oscillating pattern. The full May sortie sequence now reads: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4. With 7 days to the May 31 HIMARS payment deadline, Taiwan's Legislative Yuan Finance Committee hearings are scheduled for Monday May 25, with a floor vote expected Wednesday-Thursday May 27-28. Congressional Republicans and bipartisan members pushed back sharply against the $14B pause, with the PORCUPINE Act (passed House Foreign Affairs Committee 45-0) requiring advance notification before any arms delivery delay. The interlocking pressure triangle — $14B package frozen, FMS pause for Iran operations, Elbridge Colby Beijing visit blocked by China as leverage — represents the most complex arms ambiguity Taiwan has faced in the post-summit period. Beijing's simultaneous four-sector ADIZ surge and diplomatic pressure on the arms sale suggests coordinated signaling tied to the HIMARS budget timeline.
